findings.explanation: Inventory records show a large delivery of 300 units on the spike date 2025-02-03, compared to 100 units on prior days, with no stockout hours. This suggests the sales spike was enabled by increased availability rather than unmet demand.
Order records on the spike date show one very large order of 200 units among many 10-unit orders, indicating that a single large order contributed significantly to the sales spike.

limitations: No promotions were recorded during the period, so promotion influence is unlikely but cannot be absolutely ruled out if unrecorded.
Weather conditions were stable and typical with light rain and no deviation from prior days, so weather association is unsupported.
Comparison product sales were not examined, so relative category or store-wide effects are unknown.
The analysis is limited to three days and one store-product combination, limiting generalizability.
No customer or marketing data beyond promotions and orders is available to explain demand drivers.
assessment.nextQuestion: Was there any marketing or external event on 2025-02-03 that could explain the large single order or increased availability?
